title: 2026.3.7 US Market Close | Market plunges on stagflation fears amid recession worries and surging oil prices
description:
On March 7th, the New York stock market was gripped by fears of stagflation, driven by a major employment shock and soaring oil prices due to geopolitical risks in the Middle East. Investor sentiment soured rapidly on the worst-case combination of recession fears and re-ignited inflation, sending all major indices sharply lower at the closing bell.

- Dow Jones: Down 0.95% - Weighed down by weak employment data and recession concerns fueled by surging oil prices.
- S&P 500: Down 1.33% - Pressured by widespread stagflation fears across the market.
- Nasdaq: Tumbled 1.59% - A broad risk-off sentiment spread, hitting tech stocks particularly hard.

Key Issues:
- Employment Shock and Recession Fears: February's non-farm payrolls unexpectedly fell by 92,000, starkly contrasting with expectations of a 59,000 gain. The unemployment rate also rose to 4.4%, dominating the market with concerns of an economic hard landing.
- Surging Oil Prices and Inflation Concerns: As conflict in the Middle East effectively halted passage through the Strait of Hormuz, West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil prices skyrocketed over 10% in a single day, surpassing $91 per barrel.
- The Rise of the Stagflation Scenario: The simultaneous occurrence of employment data signaling an economic slowdown and a surge in oil prices fueling inflation spread fears of the worst-case scenario: a stagnant economy coupled with rising prices.
- The Fed's Policy Dilemma: The conflicting needs to cut interest rates to stimulate the economy and to prevent a resurgence of inflation led to a prevailing analysis that the Fed is caught in a difficult bind.

Key Stocks:
- Applied Materials (AMAT): Dropped over 6% as China-related geopolitical risks resurfaced, including a 'suspended export denial order' as part of an agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce.
- Delta Air Lines, United Airlines: Fell more than 3% as airline stocks took a direct hit from mounting concerns over cost pressures from the spike in jet fuel prices.
